subject: Selene3b elevated 5xx spike — mitigation & follow-up
messages:

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Selene3b elevated 5xx spike — mitigation & follow-up

Hi Diana —

We’re reaching out to let you know we observed an elevated rate of 5xx errors and timeouts on the Selene3b model running in your dedicated pool starting ~08:50 PT. The impact we see: increased generation failures on the /v1/generate and /v1/chat endpoints for your account (request ids attached below).

What we’ve done so far:
- Temporarily routed new traffic to Selene3b-reduced-ctx (compat fallback) to keep throughput while we investigate.
- Increased autoscaler headroom for your pool.
- Flagged suspicious scheduling changes and captured request traces.

Immediate ask from you: can you share any example request ids or a sample payload if possible? I attached a brief log snippet we captured from the gateway (selene_incident_log_snippet.txt) for reference.

We’ll update in this thread with root cause and ETA for full recovery. Sorry for the disruption — we know any generation failures are disruptive for you.

– Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference

We started seeing failed generations around 08:55 PT. Affected flows are our batch summarization job and the user-facing chat endpoint (both using Selene3b). Sample request ids: req_4f5b2e, req_4f5b3a, req_4f5b8c. Errors are "5XX: model-unavailable" and occasional websocket disconnects.

Attached is one full request + response sample from our side (bh_error_sample.json). The client impact: intermittent failures for ~20% of requests; retries workaround but increases latency. Can you provide an ETA for a permanent fix? We may need to throttle certain paths if this continues.

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 30 Nov 2028 15:15:03 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Selene3b elevated 5xx spike — mitigation & follow-up

Summary of findings so far (short):
- Root cause: a scheduling regression introduced in a scaling patch caused KV-cache index misalignment for certain sequence-length transitions (> 2048 tokens) on Selene3b. When sequences cross chunk boundaries, some GPU workers attempted to access stale KV offsets and returned internal 5xx errors.
- Why it affected Blue Horizon: their batch job frequently mixes short and long sequences in the same batch; this triggers the misalignment more often.
- What we did: rolled back the scheduling patch (deployed 12:30 PT), forced a warm restart of the affected pool and applied a hotfix to validate KV indices before access.
- Current customer-facing state: routing back to primary Selene3b (started 14:40 PT). Error rate for BH has dropped to <1% over the last 30min; we continue to monitor.

Next steps:
1) Ops will keep the enhanced KV validation flag enabled for 24h.
2) Engineering will run a regression test matrix (mixed-length sequences) and include it in CI. ETA for full sign-off: 48 hours.
3) Customer postmortem draft and suggested credits for affected usage — Rafael, please propose comms and a goodwill credit.

Attached: selene_hotfix_patch.diff (patch summary).

— Monica
Monica Patel
Sr. Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Selene3b elevated 5xx spike — mitigation & follow-up

Hi Diana — quick update and closure for the incident today.

Status:
- Root cause identified as a KV-cache index misalignment triggered by mixed-length batches; a scheduling rollback + hotfix was deployed and we validated the pool.
- We routed traffic back to primary Selene3b at 14:40 PT; observed error rate for your account dropped to <1% in the following hours.

What we recommend for you:
- If you can, separate long-batch jobs from short interactions while we push the CI regression (24–48h).
- If separation isn’t possible, we can continue running the KV validation flag for the next 72h to reduce risk.

Compensation & follow-up:
- We’ll propose a 10% credit on affected usage for the 4-hour window with elevated errors (details in a short postmortem).
- Full postmortem draft and ticket (INC-7894) are in the linked Drive folder: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/selene3b-incident-20281130.

Please let me know if you’d like a short call tomorrow to go over the postmortem and the credit. Thanks for the patience and the quick sample — that sped up triage.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
